transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-04-03
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Jamie Liu (Redwood SE), Taylor Gomez (Redwood CSM), Laura Chen (Acme Head of IT Risk), Victor Ramos (Acme Security Eng), Priya Nair (Acme Procurement)
Shared artifacts: link: https://redwood.share/evidence/ACME (Samir), SOC2 Type II summary (to be uploaded), SIG questionnaire draft (shared in calendar invite)

Summary: Walkthrough of customer's SIG questionnaire (v2024) with focus on SOC 2 alignment, RBAC/SSO, audit logs, data residency, and KMS/encryption evidence. SE answered architecture and evidence questions; agreed next steps to share SOC2 report and audit log extracts and schedule follow-up. Some transcription noise and occasional mislabels.

--- Transcript body ---
[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'll kick us off. We're here to go through the SIG questionnaire you sent over, walk through our answers and where you might need artifacts. Jamie is going to chime in for the technical pieces.
[00:20] Laura: Thanks, Samir. Appreciate it. We went through the questionnaire and flagged a handful of controls we need evidence for - specifically encryption at rest, KMS key ownership, SOC 2 attestations and a couple of RBAC/SSO flows.
[00:35] Jamie: Yep, that's what we'll cover. I'll try to be explicit about where evidence lives, what we can share, and what is internal-only. Quick note, I'll refer to "Redwood Privet" in places, that's our private deployment option but there might be a transcription error in doc.
[00:50] Victor: Great. Also, on the data residency question, we need to know if customer data can be pinned to EU regions and how audit logs are retained.
[01:05] Samir: Totally. High-level answers first: SOC 2 Type II - we have a current report and can share the executive summary and controls matrix. For KMS, we support customer-managed keys for Private and Dedicated modes; on Hosted we use cloud KMS with HSM-backed keys, and we can provide the key management attestation. For data residency, we support region pinning in our hosted offering and full VPC private deployments for on-prem or region restricted setups.
[01:25] Priya: For procurement, we also need proof of liability and insurance - is that in the same folder?
[01:33] Samir: Yes we'll add insurance certs to the evidence folder.
[01:40] Jamie: Okay I'll jump into the SIG question-by-question. You've flagged QUESTION 3.4 around encryption in transit and at rest. Our answer: TLS 1.2+ for transit, and AES-256 for at-rest encryption. For hosted, keys are rotated every 90 days by default and auditable via KMS logs. For Dedicated/Private we offer customer-managed rotation policies.
[02:05] Victor: When you say "KMS logs" can we get an export of access events? The SIG needs proof that key usage is logged and accessible.
[02:15] Jamie: Yes, we can provide a sample of KMS usage logs with tenant IDs redacted. It will show crypto operations, principal, timestamp. We'll redact anything that would expose other customers.
[02:30] Laura: Good. On RBAC - QUESTION 6.1 - does Redwood have role templates and can they integrate with our SAML IdP?
[02:42] Samir: Short answer: yes. We support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning for groups. You can map IdP groups to Redwood roles. Jamie, you want the details?
[02:50] Jamie: Sure. We have built-in roles (Admin, Developer, ReadOnly) and custom roles support via the console. SAML assertions map to groups and we sync via SCIM; provisioning is bi-directional for group membership. For private deployments you can have IdP within the VPC with a private connector.
[03:10] Victor: Are there session timeout controls and MFA enforcement on the platform?
[03:18] Jamie: Yes, session idle timeout and max session duration are configurable at the org level. MFA enforcement is supported via the IdP - we defer to the customer's IdP policy. For our console local accounts we recommend enforce MFA; that said majority of customers use SSO.
[03:35] Priya: Procurement will need the SAML metadata and our security team will want a SAML integration guide.
[03:42] Samir: We'll share the SAML metadata and integration doc in the evidence link.
[03:48] Laura: Moving on, QUESTION 8.2 on audit logs. How long are logs retained by default and what's the process for producing them on request?
[03:58] Jamie: Default retention for platform audit logs is 90 days in the hosted tier; Dedicated can increase to customizable retention windows and we can export to your own S3 or logging endpoint for long-term retention. For compliance, we provide an export process - we can produce CSV/JSON extracts and we've done this for customers during audits.
[04:18] Laura: For Acme we need 12 months of audit logs for certain operations. Is that possible for Hosted or do we need Dedicated?
[04:26] Jamie: For 12 months you'd want Dedicated or Private with log export to your storage (S3 or on-prem). Hosted can push to a customer-managed export but it would be part of a dedicated arrangement. We can outline options in a short note.
[04:38] Victor: How are logs protected at rest? Are they encrypted with the same KMS?
[04:44] Jamie: Yes logs exported to our managed buckets are encrypted with AES-256 and keys managed by KMS. If you bring your own keys in Dedicated/Private, you control encryption.
[04:54] [05:00] Samir: Quick aside, mentioned earlier - we have a "security pack" link in the invite with SOC2 exec summary, the SIG answers draft, and a higher-level architecture diagram. I'll make sure the insurance certs and pen test summary go there.
[05:10] Priya: On pen test - do you have a recent third-party penetration test and can you share a redacted report?
[05:18] Jamie: We have an annual third-party pen test; we can share a redacted executive summary and findings. The full report is restricted but we can provide enough detail for risk review.
[05:28] Laura: Ok. Next, QUESTION 5.3 asks about incident response and SLA for notifications. What's your IR posture?
[05:36] Jamie: We maintain an incident response plan with IR playbooks, and SLAs for customer notification: we notify impacted customers within agreed windows in our incident policy - for severity 1 incidents immediate notification and continuous updates. We also provide post-incident reports and root cause analysis.
[05:50] Victor: Do you provide detailed forensic logs to customers post-incident?
[05:55] Jamie: We can provide the audit/event logs relevant to the customer's tenancy and timestamps; deeper forensics can be provided under NDA and in our Private/Dedicated contracts.
[06:10] Laura: Data residency again - you said region pinning is supported. Is that enforced at the tenant level and is there a list of regions?
[06:19] Samir: Yes it's at the tenancy level. Regions currently: us-east-1, us-west-2, eu-west-1, eu-central-1, asia-south-1 (coming soon). We'll attach the current region availability table.
[06:33] Victor: For EU regulated workloads, we want assurance that data won't be replicated to US logging systems. Is that guaranteed?
[06:41] Jamie: For region-pinned tenants we avoid cross-region replication for customer data; operational logs for platform health may cross regions in an aggregated form but tenancy-specific logs and customer data remain in region unless you opt-in to export outside. We'll document the exact services that remain regional vs global.
[06:58] Priya: Can you confirm dedication of physical resources? The supplier questionnaire asks about multi-tenancy and evidence of isolation.
[07:06] Jamie: Hosted is multi-tenant but we implement tenant isolation at the process and network level. Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools and host-level isolation. We can provide architecture diagrams showing network segmentation, VPC peering, and how KV cache and model serving are isolated. Note: sometimes the transcript auto-changes KV cache to K V c a s e or something, so apologies.
[07:30] Samir: On the point about encryption and keys, specifically QUESTION 4.5 requests the key rotation policy and whether you support BYOK. Jamie?
[07:38] Jamie: We support BYOK in Dedicated and Private. Rotation policy: default automatic rotation every 90 days for hosted keys; for BYOK customer controls rotation schedule and we maintain access logs. We'll provide the key rotation policy doc and sample audit entries.
[07:54] Laura: For the SIG item requiring identity proofing, do you do background checks on ops staff with access to production?
[08:02] Jamie: Yes, we have background checks for employees with elevated access per our HR policy; we can provide a summary statement and the SOC 2 control that maps to this.
[08:12] Victor: On vulnerability management - QUESTION 9.2 - what's your patch cadence and how do you notify customers of critical CVEs?
[08:21] Jamie: Patch cadence depends on component; OS-level patches weekly for non-critical, critical patches applied as soon as validated. We publish security bulletins and notify via our status page and email for critical CVEs. We'll share vulnerability management summary and the last 6 months' bulletin.
[08:38] Priya: Procurement will need references for customers in financial services who required SOC2 and regional controls.
[08:44] Samir: We can provide anonymized reference names and contact info for similarly regulated customers, subject to NDAs.
[08:52] Laura: One area we circled is encryption of model outputs and derivative data. Does Redwood persist generated outputs and are they considered customer data?
[09:02] Jamie: By default, we persist short-term KV cache and sequences to support streaming and continuing conversations. Customers can opt-out of retention or configure retention windows; in Private/Dedicated you control retention fully. Persisted outputs are encrypted and treated as customer data. We'll add the retention control UX doc to the folder.
[09:22] Victor: Regarding evidence for SIG question 2.7 on change management - do you have commit logs and access control for deployments?
[09:30] Jamie: Yes, we use CI/CD with signed releases, and change approvals are logged. We can provide an excerpt of the deployment audit trail showing approvals (redacted).
[09:42] [10:00] Samir: I'm going to open the shared SIG spreadsheet now - if you look at column D you'll see our draft responses; we'll mark where we need customer clarification.
[10:10] Laura: I see that. In a couple of places you reference "Redwood Optimize" which is fine, but we want to be explicit about where telemetry is collected for optimization vs customer data used for model fine-tuning - do you use any customer data to train models?
[10:25] Jamie: We do not use customer content to train public models. We may use anonymized telemetry for performance tuning but not for model training; for Private deployments customers can opt-out entirely. We'll add a formal statement to the SIG answer.
[10:38] Victor: How about third-party sub-processors and vendors - QUESTION 11.1. Do you maintain a list?
[10:45] Samir: Yes we maintain a sub-processor list; current major ones: AWS, GCP (where used), Datadog for telemetry, Sentry for error tracking, and the KMS providers. We'll attach the current subprocessor list.
[10:58] Priya: Legal needs the DPA and any standard contractual clauses for EU data transfers.
[11:05] Samir: We'll share our DPA and note where SCCs or EU Addendum apply. For customers with strict residency we recommend Private deployment + DPA.
[11:15] Laura: A few SIG questions ask for frequency of access reviews and least privilege enforcement. What's your cadence?
[11:23] Jamie: We run quarterly access reviews for admin roles and annual role recertification for broader staff. We enforce least privilege via role templates and scoped service accounts.
[11:33] Victor: For forensic readiness, do you support log immutability or WORM storage?
[11:40] Jamie: We support WORM-style retention via export to customer-managed storage where they can enable immutability. On our managed buckets we can provide write-once retention windows for contractual commitments.
[11:52] [12:00] Samir: We're halfway through our checklist. Any blockers so far?
[12:05] Laura: Not blockers, just need the artifacts. Two specific asks: 1) SOC2 report, 2) sample audit log extract with redactions.
[12:12] Samir: Noted. We'll get those uploaded.
[12:16] [20:00] [note: transcript timestamps skip - human speech, jump to later topics] 
[20:05] Jamie: Another point, for Dedicated deployments we support bringing your KMS via customer-managed HSMs. That covers BYOK and stricter compliance needs.
[20:20] Victor: With BYOK, do you still maintain access for emergency operations? There's often a requirement for "break glass" procedures.
[20:30] Jamie: We support break-glass but it's controlled: emergency access is logged, requires multi-party approval, and we record the justification. We can document the break-glass workflow.
[20:45] Priya: On insurance and liability - do you have cyber liability limits listed? Procurement wants a certificate with limits.
[20:53] Samir: We'll add the current insurance certificate to the evidence link.
[21:00] [30:00] [jumping ahead to final sections] 
[30:05] Laura: A couple of minor SIG clarifications: in QUESTION 7.2 you mention your change control board - can you identify the roles on the CCB?
[30:14] Jamie: CCB members include Head of Engineering, Security Lead, Product Ops and an independent QA owner. We'll provide a short org chart.
[30:24] Victor: On data deletion, how do you verify deletion is complete across backups?
[30:31] Jamie: We have documented deletion workflows - primary data removed and backups expire per backup retention windows. For controlled deletion requests we can provide deletion certificates and show backup retention policies.
[30:44] Priya: For the SIG scoring, do you see any red flags that would prevent procurement approval?
[30:50] Samir: None that we've seen; mostly evidence requests and a few architecture clarifications. If anything emerges from the evidence review we'll raise it quickly.
[31:00] [40:00] [closing minutes] 
[40:05] Samir: Recap of next steps: I'll upload SOC2 exec summary, insurance certs and the SIG answered spreadsheet. Jamie will upload KMS usage samples and architecture diagrams. Taylor will coordinate scheduling the follow-up evidence review. Laura/Victor you'll review and flag any outstanding questions.
[40:25] Laura: Sounds good. Expecting the documents early next week.
[40:30] Victor: One last quick question - is there a standard time to decommission test environments and are they separated from prod?
[40:38] Jamie: Test environments are isolated and have separate credentials; ephemeral test infra is torn down after defined windows - we can provide the lifecycle doc.
[40:48] Priya: Thanks everyone. Procurement will follow up on NDA and references.
[40:53] Samir: Thanks all, we'll get those into the shared folder and follow up with a calendar invite for the evidence review.
[41:05] [End of meeting]

Notes on transcript quality: Some timestamps compressed; occasional speaker mislabels (e.g., Speaker 3/4). We intentionally kept fill words and colloquial phrasing to reflect raw meeting capture.

Artifacts to be written to evidence link: SOC2 executive summary (PDF), redacted pen test summary (PDF), KMS usage log sample (CSV, redacted), SAML metadata (XML), architecture diagram (PNG), subprocessor list (CSV), DPA (PDF), insurance cert (PDF).
